title: A constructed quotient tower with normalized scalar transposes
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative ring, J an ideal, and U an object of its coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Use the actual scalar reductions R_n, restrictions S_n, and Hom successors of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Each scalar extension admits a unique adjunction with restriction whose unit is adicFiniteUnit, normalized on K-flat representatives by insertion of one. For any M define t_n:S_(n+1) R_(n+1) M -> S_n R_n M as the adj_n transpose of HomStep applied to the counit at R_(n+1) M. Then for every T and f:R_(n+1) T -> R_(n+1) M, transpose_(n+1)(f) followed by t_n equals transpose_n(HomStep(f)). The units form a cone with vertex M over the tower defined by these transitions. No completeness or Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Derive the ordinary tensor/restriction adjunction along an arbitrary coefficient map using flat-term K-flat resolutions. Transport its universally specified derived pair to ConstantCompletion.extend. The universal comparison on representatives identifies its unit with the existing adicFiniteUnit. This is a unique adjunction, since its unit determines it.

Define the successor as the transpose of the Hom successor applied to the preceding counit. Write f as extension of its transpose followed by the counit. Naturality of the balancing comparison moves that transpose through HomStep; naturality of the next adjunction proves the displayed equation. This is the Lean proof adicResidueAdjointStep_transpose.

Apply the transpose equation to the identity: HomStep preserves the identity by cancellation of the balancing isomorphism, so the units commute with the successors. Functor.ofOpSequence and NatTrans.ofOpSequence construct the tower and cone.

theorem adicResidueAdjointStep_transpose
    (T M : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U) (n : ℕ)
    (f : (adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U (n + 1)).obj T ⟶
      (adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U (n + 1)).obj M) :
    (adicResidueScalarAdjunction.{u, v} X J U (n + 1)).homEquiv T _ f ≫
        adicResidueAdjointStep.{u, v} X J U M n =
      (adicResidueScalarAdjunction.{u, v} X J U n).homEquiv T _
        (adicResidueHomStep.{u, v} X J U T M n f)
